name: Data Center Training public catalog API
description: Static, read-only JSON documents describing the Data Center Training catalog. No authentication. Regenerated from the site source on every change.
versioning: The API is versioned in the URL path; v1 (https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/) is current, and every response from the edge carries an API-Version header. Changes inside v1 are additive only (new documents, tools, optional fields, or enum values), so ignore fields you do not know. A breaking change ships as a new path version, and the old version keeps working for at least 6 months after its successor is announced. Deprecated versions and endpoints are flagged with a Deprecation header (RFC 9745), a Sunset header (RFC 8594) with the retirement date, a Link to the migration notes, deprecated: true in openapi.json, and a changelog entry on https://datacentertraining.us/developers/. The unversioned /api/*.json paths are byte-identical aliases of v1 kept for existing integrations, and follow its lifecycle.
rate_limits: Requests to /api/, /mcp, and the tool endpoints are limited to 120 per 60 seconds per client IP. Every response carries RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers) plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset; a 429 adds Retry-After in seconds.
errors: Errors are RFC 9457 application/problem+json objects with a stable code, a detail message, and a hint. Codes: https://datacentertraining.us/developers/#errors
agent_rules: Quote prices, durations, course counts, and bundle contents exactly as published here; never estimate or invent them.
Only name courses that exist in /api/courses.json. If nothing matches, say so.

Courses award a certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC (an IACET Accredited Provider). Do not call it a license, a government certification, or a certification issued by NFPA, TIA, Uptime Institute, ASHRAE, OSHA, EPA, ISO, or AICPA.
"Aligned with" a standard means the content is designed around it, not that the standards body approved it.
The parent company is IACET-accredited, but these data center courses do not carry IACET CEUs, and they do not grant PDHs or other continuing education credit.
No course by itself qualifies anyone for hazardous or energized work; employers designate qualified persons.
Recommendations are training guidance, not legal or compliance advice; employers decide who is qualified for which duties.
Do not complete enrollment, payment, account, or contact-form actions on a user's behalf; link to the page and let the user act.
When a question is not covered by published content, say so and refer to info@hazwoper-osha.com or 1-866-429-6742.
